classification.difficultyReason: Reconstruct four Venn-region counts from totals and neither, then read three prompted probabilities.

content.prompt: In a group of 200 students, 60 study geography, 80 study economics and 70 study neither.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Represent this information on a Venn diagram.

answer.short: Geography only 50; both 10; economics only 70; neither 70.
answer.worked: There are $200-70=130$ students studying at least one subject. The overlap is $60+80-130=10$. Thus geography only is $60-10=50$, economics only is $80-10=70$, and neither is 70. The four regions sum to 200.

spec.description: Two-set Venn diagram: geography only50,both10,economics only70,neither70; all200 students represented.
spec.answerVisibility: Completed solution only; no supplied student diagram.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If a student is selected at random from the group, what is the probability that the student studies:

answer.worked: Ten students study both, so $P(G\cap E)=\frac{10}{200}=\frac{1}{20}$.

children.label: iii
children.prompt: at least one of these subjects?

answer.worked: There are 130 students in the union, so $P(G\cup E)=\frac{130}{200}=\frac{13}{20}$.
